generator.program.note: The lineage's own program (growth plan G2.3a), on the broadleaf base: it gives the values its species leave unset, which the broadleaf program gave as defaults until then.

traits.note: Jepson eFlora's account of the family, as search results quote it (the page itself was not read): calyx teeth (2)5; corolla small, radial, rotate, (3-4)5-lobed; stamens 5, rarely 4, on the corolla; ovary more or less inferior, 1- or 3- to 5-chambered. Abrams and Ferris (volume 4, read in full) give the elders' corolla rotate and regular and the ovary 3- to 5-celled.

traits.leaf_arrangement.note: Hutchinson (vol. 1, 2nd ed., 1959), family 306 Adoxaceae (moschatel), with the elders and viburnums he still keeps in Caprifoliaceae, which APG joins as Viburnaceae (Adoxaceae): leaves opposite; fruit a drupe.

traits.fruit_type.note: Hutchinson (vol. 1, 2nd ed., 1959), family 306 Adoxaceae (moschatel), with the elders and viburnums he still keeps in Caprifoliaceae, which APG joins as Viburnaceae (Adoxaceae): leaves opposite; fruit a drupe.

traits.rosette.note: APweb, Dipsacales page (read 2026-10-16): Viburnum and Sambucus shrubs/trees; no order value proposed because Caprifoliaceae herbs often form basal rosettes.

traits.leaf_margin.note: Wikipedia Viburnum (read 2026-10-17) (about 165 species, most of the family): margins toothed or lobed, though it also calls them entire; Wikipedia Sambucus: leaflets with serrated margins.

traits.leaf_incision.note: Wikipedia Viburnum (read 2026-10-17): simple leaves, some toothed or lobed (lobed in V. opulus group). Sambucus compound.
